TunnelLock creates a separate “secure space” on your phone. Apps you put in it can only use the internet through the VPN. If the VPN drops even for a moment, Android itself cuts their internet; the app is not closed and works again once the connection is back.
1. Tap “Create secure space” and confirm Android\'s screens.
2. TunnelLock opens inside the secure space (with a briefcase badge).
3. Under Servers, add a V2Ray link or a subscription link.
4. Add apps to the secure space from this outer app (without the briefcase).
The secure space is being set up…

• Apps in the secure space can only reach the internet through this app's VPN.
• While the service runs, the tunnel is always up. If the server drops, packets are discarded inside the tunnel and nothing leaves through the normal network.
• If the connection drops while you use an app, the app stays open and only loses internet; it works again once the connection is back.
• If the app itself is closed or killed, Android's “Always-on VPN” + “Block connections without VPN” cuts the secure space off completely.
• When you disconnect yourself (and “Pause apps” is on), protected apps can't be opened until you connect again.
• If the server stops answering and “Automatic server switch” is on, another working server from your list takes over.
• If “Automatic subscription update” is on, subscriptions are refreshed every 12 hours.
• Apps marked “Always openable” can be opened while disconnected, but have no internet.
• Your normal apps (outside the secure space) are not affected.

TunnelLock connects to SSH itself and sends the apps\' traffic through it. SSH carries TCP only: voice and video calls that need UDP may not work (most apps fall back to TCP).
Private key (optional, instead of or with the password)
Server key fingerprint, optional (SHA256:...). If empty, the first one seen is remembered.
The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
Save battery with the screen off

With the screen off the connection is checked every minute instead of every 15 seconds, and at once when the screen comes on. A drop is then noticed up to about a minute later (apps have no internet meanwhile either; nothing gets out).
The secure space is off ("work apps" paused): protected apps cannot open and TunnelLock does not run inside it (no connection, no update checks). Turn on "Work apps" in Quick Settings.
Fake location for the secure space

One fixed location is given to every app in the secure space (not a separate one per app; without root Android allows just one fake-location app). This is the device GPS, not the IP; the IP is set by each app\'s server. For it to work you must pick this app as the "mock location app" in Developer Options.
